title: From prediction to action
question: How did learning move from prediction toward physical action?
scope: Historical schematic; the time axis widens after 2005 and spacing is not a uniform duration scale.

steps.title: Feedback before learning
steps.description: The upper lane begins with feedback and programmed robots. Acting on the world predates learned perception or learned motor outputs.

steps.title: Representations enter the machine
steps.description: The lower lane traces learning to predict, including ALVINN and deep networks on ImageNet. Its convergence with control is a systems history, not a claim that every robot followed one sequence.

steps.title: Learning reaches motion proposals
steps.description: The merged lane marks visuomotor policies, chunked and diffusion policies, and VLA models. Learned outputs increasingly specify motion that the surrounding system must check.

steps.title: Identify the architectural handoff
steps.description: Read the band separately from the milestones: perception feeds hand-written planners, then learned motor commands and pretrained proposers appear. A learned proposal still needs permission before physical work.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: Robot models train on a sliver of frontier compute
question: Does the robotics compute record match the language-model scaling record?
scope: Epoch estimates and database tags describe the plotted record, not all private training runs or a causal experiment on action quality.

steps.title: Read the units before comparing height
steps.description: Training compute is plotted on a logarithmic FLOP axis. Equal vertical gaps indicate multiplicative ratios, not equal additions of compute.

steps.title: Separate model outputs
steps.description: Filled green markers are robotics models; open squares identify video world models. Predicting video is not the same output as generating robot actions.

steps.title: Compare contemporaneous records
steps.description: The labeled action policies sit below the largest language-model estimates in nearby years. The chart documents a compute gap; it does not show that simply increasing compute would establish safe action.

steps.title: Keep the scope of the evidence
steps.description: These points are database estimates for recorded models. The action-policy versus world-model distinction prevents a high-compute video model from silently standing in for learned motor control.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: The closed causal loop
question: Where does a learned output become an irreversible physical action?
scope: Architectural comparison, not a timed simulation. Permission and the causal boundary perform different jobs.

steps.title: A prediction can stop at information
steps.description: The advisory path ends at a prediction across an informational interface. This drawing does not give that prediction authority to deliver force.

steps.title: A proposal is checked
steps.description: The policy sends a proposal to the permission path. This separation determines what may be admitted; the learned model is not itself the final authority.

steps.title: Admission reaches hardware
steps.description: An admitted command crosses the red causal boundary into actuators. Current produces force and motion in the physical plant; those effects cannot be recalled like an unused prediction.

steps.title: Action changes the next input
steps.description: The return path closes through the world and sensors. A policy therefore encounters observations shaped by previously admitted actions.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: Delay travel and braking travel against speed
question: How does speed divide the stopping budget between delay and braking?
scope: Elementary illustrative constant-deceleration model; no measured chassis stop or complete safety margin is claimed. Later allowances still have to be added.

steps.title: Delay is distance
steps.description: The brown term is v τ_delay: the plant keeps moving before braking begins. Reducing latency contracts this term without making the braking term disappear.

steps.title: Braking grows faster with speed
steps.description: The blue term is v²/(2a_brake). Doubling speed multiplies this term by four under the stated constant-deceleration assumptions.

steps.title: Find which term dominates
steps.description: At the marked crossover the two travel terms are equal. Above that speed the quadratic braking contribution exceeds delay travel.

steps.title: A spare difference is not a qualified margin
steps.description: The black curve sums both terms; the drive-limit marker lies below the clear-distance threshold in this elementary calculation. Localization, protective allowance, tracking error, and jerk-limited braking still belong in the eventual budget.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Three machine classes
question: Which physical margin does each machine class spend?
scope: The three classes isolate dominant constraints; a real machine can face all three simultaneously.

steps.title: Momentum spends clearance
steps.description: Class 1 combines travel during delay with braking travel. A software delay consumes physical distance before deceleration can stop the moving mass.

steps.title: Small displacement can mean large force
steps.description: Class 2 shows a compliant contact with F = k_contact Δx. A small position error against a stiff object can spend the available force and deformation margin.

steps.title: Holding still still consumes a budget
steps.description: Class 3 balances input and removed heat against thermal capacitance. Sustained current can heat a winding even when motion is absent, while the supply must retain headroom for fallback.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: The physical AI scope test
question: What combination makes a system physical AI in this book?
scope: This is a scope test, not a safety certification. An independent veto remains compatible with delegated authority.

steps.title: Learning alone does not define the scope
steps.description: The upper circle supplies the learned component. Its pairwise overlaps still omit one of the other requirements.

steps.title: A person can retain action approval
steps.description: Advisory systems join learning and physical feedback while a person approves actions. Digital autonomy instead joins learning and delegated authority without the consequential physical feedback required here.

steps.title: Automatic physical control need not be learned
steps.description: Classical control joins physical feedback with delegated authority. Without a learned component, it falls outside this book’s three-way scope test.

steps.title: All three meet at the center
steps.description: Physical AI has a learned component, consequential physical feedback, and delegated actuation authority. The independent permission path may veto proposals inside this intersection.

title: The five-level machine
question: How do proposal authority and physical timescales fit the five-level machine?
scope: Rates are pinned reference-design examples, not universal requirements. Governance encloses the lifecycle rather than adding a sixth level.

steps.title: A fast proposer is still a proposer
steps.description: The Brain band lists distinct rates for intent, chunk renewal, and setpoints. The gap below it marks the proposal boundary: the Brain may propose, while the permission path below decides admission.

steps.title: Admission has its own execution path
steps.description: The Nervous System carries lease and fallback checks on a reference permission loop. Its job cannot be delegated to an unqualified learned output.

steps.title: Permission becomes work below the seam
steps.description: The Body contains drives and windings; the Boundary names register writes and sensor capture. The World continues evolving through contact, friction, payload, and people. These are distinct layers even when coupled tightly.

steps.title: Governance surrounds the machine
steps.description: The dashed envelope spans the lifecycle. A governance chapter does not identify a new physical tier or inherit a control-loop rate.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: The spine of the book
question: Which records connect physical limits, learned competence, and live permission?
scope: The record chain describes obligations and consumers, not proof that the running example already has qualified evidence.

steps.title: Start with the plant’s limits
steps.description: The limit record feeds the handoff record. Physical capabilities and operating premises must be explicit before downstream evidence can rely on them.

steps.title: Record what the proposer demonstrated
steps.description: Provenance, policy manifest, and evaluation record form the competence strand. A model checkpoint alone does not carry the tested operating conditions.

steps.title: Join evidence to today’s proposal
steps.description: Observation contract, belief record, intent lease, and trajectory feed enforcement and placement. Live observations and proposals must meet the previously established limits and competence conditions.

steps.title: Authority must remain justified
steps.description: The lower chain carries authority, fault, release, approval, and residual claims. A later release consumes these records; it does not erase the permission checks needed for each action.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry. Peer audit: tightened bounds against full-size canonical image and corrected label or terminal-record coverage.

title: Open vs. closed loop divergence
question: Why can a small replay error coexist with a physical clearance violation?
scope: Fixed one-degree heading example for the navigation stack, not a simulation of the latch policy or a general divergence rate.

steps.title: Replay returns to recorded states
steps.description: The top panel repeatedly supplies the recorded centerline state. A small angular MSE does not make the candidate’s output determine its next input.

steps.title: The plant accumulates displacement
steps.description: The lower panel applies the fixed heading to actual forward travel. Lateral position grows with distance because the next state retains the consequence of prior motion.

steps.title: Read the physical failure threshold
steps.description: The rising line reaches the dashed side-clearance line at the marked point. The physical question is whether clearance remains, not whether recorded-state angular loss looks small.

steps.title: Match the test to the deployed loop
steps.description: The panels differ in feedback, not in the declared heading offset. Closed-loop evaluation is needed to observe states produced by the candidate’s own admitted actions.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Evaluation evidence regimes
question: What does each evaluation regime leave untested?
scope: The two axes classify evidence; moving right or upward does not turn one regime into complete deployment proof.

steps.title: Replay fixes the observations
steps.description: In recorded replay, policy outputs are scored against a logged sequence. The output cannot change the next recorded state, so replay cannot expose drift caused by the candidate’s own actions.

steps.title: Simulation closes a modeled loop
steps.description: The simulated plant feeds candidate actions back into subsequent state. The explicit f_sim ≠ f_real warning preserves the reality gap.

steps.title: Real hardware can still follow another controller
steps.description: Shadow mode observes live hardware, but the baseline controller drives it. Logged candidate actions do not determine the state distribution.

steps.title: A constrained test stops at its envelope
steps.description: The permission path allows live candidate motion within the test envelope. The marked boundary truncates behavior before open deployment, so the test supplies no direct evidence beyond that boundary.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: Inverting a clean record into a bound
question: Which success probabilities can twenty clean runs rule out?
scope: One-sided frequentist inversion under independent identically distributed trials; confidence is coverage of the procedure, not a posterior probability that this policy is safe.

steps.title: Ask how likely the observed record would be
steps.description: For a candidate per-run success probability p, the blue curve gives p²⁰. The vertical log scale makes very unlikely clean campaigns visible.

steps.title: Invert at the declared threshold
steps.description: The dashed α_sig line crosses the curve at the lower bound. Candidates to the left would make twenty clean runs rarer than the predeclared threshold.

steps.title: A concerning policy still fits the evidence
steps.description: The open square marks a policy failing one run in eight. It can still produce twenty clean runs often enough to sit above the rejection threshold.

steps.title: Do not turn a clean streak into certainty
steps.description: The lower bound limits what this campaign supports under its sampling model. It is neither the point estimate p = 1 nor proof across untested conditions.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Confidence bounds and testing budgets
question: Why does each further nine of reliability cost so many trials?
scope: Zero-failure iid campaigns and one-sided Clopper–Pearson bounds. Hardware changes or drifting conditions can invalidate pooling even when the plot’s trial count grows.

steps.title: Early trials lift the floor
steps.description: The upper panel shows success lower limits rising after clean trials. Twenty successes still leave a substantial possible failure rate at the marked confidence level.

steps.title: Higher targets crowd the top
steps.description: The curves approach the 99.9 percent target slowly. A compressed success axis can hide how expensive that last gap is.

steps.title: Read the same evidence as failure
steps.description: The lower panel puts failure upper limits on log axes. Roughly one decade of additional trials buys one decade of reduction in the bound.

steps.title: Trials consume a physical test cell
steps.description: The marked budgets translate a reliability target into repeated door cycles and occupancy time. Parallel rigs can reduce elapsed time but cannot supply missing operating-condition diversity by themselves.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Miles needed to demonstrate road-vehicle reliability
question: Which reliability questions can a fleet’s mileage actually support?
scope: RAND requirements and the dated rider-only exposure are reference evidence. Crossing a bar is not a claim of measured compliance, and the three statistical questions are distinct.

steps.title: Distinguish the questions
steps.description: The legend separates a zero-failure upper bound, a rate estimate within 20 percent, and a better-than-human test at stated power. Those are different evidentiary obligations.

steps.title: Rare outcomes demand more exposure
steps.description: The fatality bars extend far beyond the corresponding injury and crash bars on the logarithmic mileage axis. A single mileage total does not imply equal certainty for all outcomes.

steps.title: Compare only the dated record
steps.description: The dashed line locates the printed rider-only exposure through January 2025. Its crossing of some crash or injury bars does not cross any fatality requirement.

steps.title: Translate exposure into a bounded claim
steps.description: The chart prices specified statistical questions; it does not show all operating domains, configurations, or failure mechanisms were tested. Those remain separate release obligations.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Standardized robotic evaluation facility
question: Locate standardized test conditions without implying deployment coverage.
scope: Keep the credited facility photograph static. The visible standardized bays ground the testing context; successful runs cannot certify glare, contaminants, or obstacles outside that arena.

title: Predict and update on the rack-end range
question: How can a tighter uncertainty bar still hide a large physical error?
scope: Scalar illustrative range estimator; bars show one modeled standard deviation, not a deterministic clearance bound or a test of every timestamp fault.

steps.title: Prediction spends uncertainty
steps.description: The prediction bar widens relative to the prior. Without a new measurement, uncertainty grows under the process model.

steps.title: Qualified measurements reduce modeled spread
steps.description: The LiDAR and stereo updates narrow the bar under their noise and alignment assumptions. The gray input bars distinguish measurement spread from the posterior spread.

steps.title: A wrong epoch biases the center
steps.description: Misdated stereo reports the same tight spread while shifting the estimate far from the true-range line. Covariance reduction alone cannot certify that timestamps and geometry were correct.

steps.title: Precision is not evidence validity
steps.description: Compare the correctly dated and misdated stereo columns. Matching bar widths do not imply matching physical accuracy; acquisition epoch is part of the measurement contract.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Three evidence epochs in one cycle
question: Why is one token sequence not one physical snapshot?
scope: Illustrative asynchronous cycle on one bounded clock; propagation reconciles epochs but does not renew the original camera evidence.

steps.title: Date the force observation
steps.description: The tactile latch marks when that force evidence was acquired. Sharing a cycle or a serialized input sequence does not make it simultaneous with the other signals.

steps.title: Use exposure time for the image
steps.description: The camera’s evidence epoch is its exposure midpoint. Arrival or publication time would conceal the motion that happened after photons were captured.

steps.title: Reconcile to the encoder epoch
steps.description: The encoder sample occurs later. Fusing at this epoch requires projecting the earlier camera state across the marked gap with a kinematic model and bounded velocity.

steps.title: Keep acquisition and estimate epochs distinct
steps.description: Propagation may date an estimate at the encoder sample, but the camera evidence remains capture-dated. A consumer still needs that original age when evaluating validity.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Manipulator kinematic frame tree and temporal dynamics
question: Why must a measured target pose stay tied to its capture epoch?
scope: The target is the capture-dated base-frame result. The dotted camera measurement is not a second parent in the transform tree.

steps.title: Geometry establishes the lever arm
steps.description: The wrist camera is mounted near the tool. A change in wrist angle can swing a fingertip by approximately r_arm Δθ_joint, even when a retained measurement has not changed.

steps.title: Every frame has one parent
steps.description: The tree runs from world through base_link and articulated links to wrist_cam and tool0. Each edge has its own kinematic, calibration, or estimation premises.

steps.title: Preserve the capture-dated result
steps.description: The target_object hangs from base_link on an edge stamped at acquisition. The dotted path records which camera measurement produced it; it does not add another transform-tree parent.

steps.title: Do not mix old measurement with current joints
steps.description: Retaining a camera-relative target and composing it with current wrist kinematics changes the time represented by the calculation. Preserve the capture epoch or propagate with a qualified motion bound.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: Transform staleness and lever-arm error at the latch-release slot
question: How does a stale camera edge become fingertip error?
scope: Illustrative geometry with zero ingestion delay to isolate one frame period; deployment must use the full capture-to-use age.

steps.title: An old edge fixes an old pose
steps.description: The pale dashed pose represents the camera edge at t₀. The tolerance circle is around the intended slot location, not around the new fingertip.

steps.title: Age permits translation
steps.description: Over Δt, bounded drift moves the wrist by v_drift Δt. The bottom arrow isolates this translational contribution.

steps.title: A small angle becomes a lever-arm sweep
steps.description: The wrist also turns by Δθ_joint = ω Δt. The fingertip is r_arm from the wrist, so rotation contributes approximately r_arm Δθ_joint.

steps.title: The clearance must cover the combined error
steps.description: The red arrow combines initial error, translation, and rotational sweep. A low ingestion delay does not remove the error accumulated since capture.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: Odometry drift against the localization bound
question: How does a localization bound become a correction-spacing requirement?
scope: Linear extrapolation of UMBmark systematic return errors from a slow laboratory path. Neither line is a qualified warehouse drift envelope.

steps.title: Normalize error by travel
steps.description: Both illustrative lines grow with distance driven. Calibration changes the systematic rate rather than making external localization unnecessary.

steps.title: Turn the error allowance into a distance
steps.description: The red line is the localization bound. Its early intersection with uncalibrated odometry shows why a fixed bound cannot simply be assumed between arbitrarily spaced corrections.

steps.title: Calibration buys limited spacing
steps.description: The calibrated crossing is only beyond the one-aisle marker. Even the optimistic systematic model does not support indefinitely accumulating dead reckoning.

steps.title: Qualify the actual machine
steps.description: Slip, payload, speed, and heading accumulation are not resolved by these straight extrapolations. The deployed correction interval must come from the machine’s own drift envelope.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Even the best odometry needs a correction within one aisle
question: How does a benchmark translation error map to a finite localization horizon?
scope: Road-driving benchmark evidence; the top-axis conversion assumes constant drift and does not predict warehouse performance. Sensor grouping is observational, not a controlled sensor comparison.

steps.title: Each dot is a method, not a trial
steps.description: The rows group ranked methods by their sensor tags. Their placement is measured benchmark translation error averaged over the stated subsequences.

steps.title: Read the multiplicative error axis
steps.description: Translation error is percent of distance on a log axis. A low percentage still accumulates physical displacement as the path grows.

steps.title: Convert error into a finite bridge
steps.description: The upper axis converts a constant error rate into travel before the 50 mm bound is spent. The shaded range is shorter than the reference aisle.

steps.title: Keep benchmark and deployment separate
steps.description: The road benchmark motivates frequent external corrections; it does not qualify correction spacing on warehouse flooring, under its payloads, or with its scene geometry.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Clearance query cost and snapshot storage by representation family
question: Why do clearance-query work and snapshot capacity constrain different choices?
scope: Counts and voxel payloads under the stated geometry, not measured latency. Header checks, metadata, active buffers, code, and validation workspace also consume resources.

steps.title: A clearance query must cover the hull
steps.description: The occupancy curves count all cells needed to certify one sphere hull, with extra tree traversal for worst-case octree scans. Finer pitch rapidly increases that work.

steps.title: A distance field changes query work
steps.description: The ESDF line holds the geometric corner-read count fixed across pitch. This removes the dense scan, but not fixed header checks or the need to qualify execution time.

steps.title: Fast lookup still needs resident data
steps.description: The lower panel prices dense voxel payload for the stopping corridor. Finer pitch raises storage even when the ESDF query itself takes the same geometric read count.

steps.title: Budget both work and capacity
steps.description: The SRAM line applies to resident storage, while the upper threshold applies to query reads. Fitting either alone does not establish that all metadata, buffers, and execution obligations fit.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Hierarchical 3D dynamic scene graph architecture
question: How do symbolic warehouse tasks stay grounded in metric geometry?
scope: A representation hierarchy, not automatic authorization: symbolic nodes do not by themselves certify collision clearance or evidence freshness.

steps.title: Begin with metric surfaces
steps.description: Layer 1 retains warehouse mesh geometry. Layer 2 extracts named objects and dynamic agents, including the mug, cage door, and person.

steps.title: Organize reachable places
steps.description: Layer 3 connects places through free-space structure. Its place nodes differ from object identities: a route connects spaces rather than treating an object label as a path.

steps.title: Compress places into task structure
steps.description: Rooms and buildings organize aisle, cross-aisle, dock, warehouse, and loading-dock relationships. This structure supports higher-level task reasoning.

steps.title: Ground a task back down
steps.description: The opposing arrows matter: abstraction compresses metric detail upward, while grounding resolves symbolic tasks toward metric coordinates. A task name is not a substitute for a current physical check.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: Free-space erosion at the rack end
question: Why can a fresh-looking map fail to certify space beside an occluded rack?
scope: The plotted erosion horizon holds the hull at its stated pose. A moving hull must be checked along its entire trajectory; unknown space is not observed free space.

steps.title: Occlusion begins at capture
steps.description: The sightline cannot see the cross aisle behind the rack. A hidden person may already occupy that unknown region; the map must not label it newly free.

steps.title: Reachable space consumes certified depth
steps.description: The dashed disc represents where the hidden person may reach under the walking-speed bound. Localization and protective clearance further reduce the depth available to the hull.

steps.title: Publication does not reset the clock
steps.description: The lower curve starts with a physical depth allowance and loses it with elapsed time. The shaded dispatch-age slice is already spent before memory receives the frame.

steps.title: Pose determines whether any horizon exists
steps.description: For the current pose the curve reaches zero at its marked horizon. Beside the rack end the side clearance certifies nothing even at capture; a faster lookup cannot restore a missing line of sight.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Belief uncertainty and invalidation horizon
question: When does a stored spatial belief stop supporting insertion motion?
scope: Deterministic illustrative error-growth bound for a latch slot. This is distinct from a Gaussian confidence interval; extrapolation supplies no new evidence.

steps.title: Begin with nonzero error
steps.description: The solid curve starts above zero and grows under bounded unobserved motion. Storage preserves the record, not its original precision.

steps.title: Validity ends at physical clearance
steps.description: The curve reaches the task-clearance threshold at the marked invalidation horizon. A required fallback must begin early enough to complete within its own qualified budget.

steps.title: A weaker model admits too long
steps.description: The dashed constant-velocity estimate grows more slowly because it omits the bounded acceleration term. Its later admission occurs when the solid bound has already exceeded clearance.

steps.title: A new estimate is not renewal
steps.description: The shaded region is expired support for this motion claim. Only qualified new evidence can renew the relevant state; refreshing a timestamp or recomputing the old prediction cannot.

review_notes: Canonical computed figure from the fresh Volume IV HTML build visually inspected; original plotted data, axes, and labels retained.

title: Spatial belief state machine and transition invariants
question: What evidence is required to restore a spatial belief to VALID?
scope: These guards govern a declared belief record. Passing time or publishing an estimate never creates a new observation.

steps.title: Occlusion changes the claim
steps.description: Occlusion moves VALID to DEGRADED. The record now relies on a declared propagation law whose growing error must remain within the allowed bound.

steps.title: An expired record supports no motion
steps.description: Reaching the error limit or leaving the validity region moves the record to EXPIRED. Keeping the record in memory does not retain its authority.

steps.title: Renewal requires physical evidence
steps.description: Both return rails require fresh evidence, the innovation gate, and a revalidated model. A newly stamped estimate alone cannot take either rail.

steps.title: Observability requires its missing constraint
steps.description: Loss of observability can occur from any of the upper states. Leaving UNOBSERVABLE requires restoring the missing constraint and passing the same evidence guard.

review_notes: Canonical original SVG and fresh-build PNG visually inspected; focus regions follow the original labels and geometry.

title: The release argument as a graph
question: Why does this apparently detailed release argument still support only REFUSE?
scope: All shown premises are illustrative, declared, or unknown; no leaf is measured on the proposed configuration.

steps.title: Decompose the actual claim
steps.description: C0 claims restricted mug delivery with stopping and contact limits. C1 splits into base stop, door latch, and mug handover; each needs its own premises.

steps.title: A value is not its evidence
steps.description: The right-hand leaves print calculations and assumptions, but their outlines carry evidence status. Read them against the legend: none is measured on this configuration.

steps.title: Other obligations remain independent
steps.description: Permission timing, braking traction, observation age, independence, and authority transfer each support distinct claims. A favorable stopping calculation cannot discharge all of them.

steps.title: A live defeater attacks a premise
steps.description: Clear oil film attacks C3’s traction assumption directly. Combined with the unqualified leaves, the graph as drawn supports REFUSE rather than a release assembled from plausible numbers.

title: Exposure licenses claims one outcome at a time
question: Why do the same fleet miles support different claims for different outcomes?
scope: Dated observational fleet estimates against a location-adjusted human benchmark. Confidence intervals and event counts remain part of every outcome claim; mileage alone is not release authorization.

steps.title: Read intervals before point estimates
steps.description: The common outcomes in panel (a) have comparatively narrow intervals. Their claim concerns those outcomes and the printed benchmark, not a single all-purpose fleet safety score.

steps.title: Rare outcomes retain large uncertainty
steps.description: The orange serious-injury and fatal outcomes rest on few observed crashes. The count labels explain why a favorable point estimate still carries a wide interval.

steps.title: Exposure narrows outcomes at different rates
steps.description: Panel (b) follows releases as rider-only miles accumulate. The injury series tightens while serious-injury intervals remain wider because severe events accumulate slowly.

steps.title: Keep each claim attached to its evidence
steps.description: A release reviewer must retain outcome, interval, operating domain, and configuration. Pooling mileage cannot turn uncertainty about rare severe outcomes into evidence already obtained for common crashes.

title: The S·P·A intersection landscape
question: Where do sensing, planning, and actuation share a physical decision?
scope: S·P·A is a diagnostic locator, not a replacement architecture or proof of safety. The central permission path is independent of the learned proposer.

steps.title: Locate the object now
steps.description: Sense carries age and location. At Sense ∩ Plan, the handoff must put the object in the current timed and framed state needed for a motion proposal.

steps.title: Check what acting changed
steps.description: Act ∩ Sense asks what changed after force and motion. Feedback needs a new physical observation, not merely a propagated estimate or a task-completion token.

steps.title: Check whether motion fits
steps.description: Plan ∩ Act asks whether the proposed path fits physical limits. A task-level goal does not establish feasible derivatives, clearance, or fallback.

steps.title: Admit only within the shared budget
steps.description: At the center, the independent permission decision checks the relevant shared physical budgets before actuation. The three interfaces locate which contract broke; none alone grants authority.
